utterances.text: Oh, yes, yes. There was one called Bjelobrk. And then there was another driver, a man called Mrdja. They changed shifts as well, you know.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you also visit the pumps with Mr. Vuleta?

utterances.speaker: BRANKO ROSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, because I was in a different shift. There was another one with me. Vuleta and I worked different shifts.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You mentioned that you were asked whether you saw any high-ranking delegations, and you said that you knew that they used to come but you didn't see --

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Let me just object to the form of the question because I think it mischaracterises it. I don't think the Court said that it was high-ranking and that's one of the issues we wanted to raise with the Court by the interpretation of the word "delegation." I don't believe the court ever mentioned that it was a high-ranking delegation. The witness if given time would explain or I believe would explain something different. But that's my objection to the form of the question.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: I have to ask, do you have any further questions?

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Yes, just two, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Sir, do you ever recall anyone -- were you ever at the camp when a delegation came from Banja Luka in mid-July 1992?

utterances.speaker: BRANKO ROSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I wasn't there then.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You also mentioned on page 26 today that the detainees received one meal a day, and then on page 36, you said that the police took them to lunch and back. Is it correct that the detainees only received one meal a day?

utterances.speaker: BRANKO ROSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Two meals. I didn't say that. They got only two meals a day. They didn't get one. That's wrong. They were given two meals a day, but not more than two.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: To your knowledge?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: This would include breakfast? Yes or no.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] They would get breakfast and supper. A rather late breakfast and supper. That's how it was. Two times a day.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: Thank you for this. I think we understood.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You said that there was around 6.000 meals prepared at the separacija.

utterances.speaker: BRANKO ROSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Isn't it true that detainees went in groups of approximately 30 people to lunch?

utterances.speaker: BRANKO ROSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, they were taken in groups because they couldn't go all at once. So one group would go, and then another. And they would take them there in a column. I saw that.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Thank you. I have no further questions. But just for the record it, may be helpful to have -- Your Honour mentioned the Cyrillic C, which looked like an O. And perhaps we can have on the record that the Cyrillic P looks like an N on Exhibit S15-16-2.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: I think we know all what is the meaning of this. Any additions in return?

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: No, Your Honour. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: No further questions. Then please understand, Mr. Rosic, we are in a hurry. In one minute, we have a plenary of the Judges, and we have to be there immediately. I have to thank you for your testimony yesterday and today. And it really assisted us in some further -- getting some further knowledge out of what happened in 1992 at the place where you worked, all these deplorable incidents, and we hope that the future of your country will be a better one than it was in 1992 and in the following period. Thank you very much for coming.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Let's hope so. Thank you, too. I have a request, Your Honour. Thank you. I have a request, Your Honour, if possible.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: If it's a very brief one.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] It is brief. I wish to visit Mr. Stakic, if that is possible, because he comes from my area, and I know him. I would like to visit him because I will see his parents when I go home, and they will ask me whether I saw their son. If you agree, that's what I want to ask. May I visit him?

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: We'll explain it to the witness, Your Honour. We apologise. We'll explain it to the witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: It's for the Defence counsel to make the necessary arrangements. Thank you, this concludes today's session. The trial stays adjourned until tomorrow, 2.15. There is no 65 ter (i) meeting tomorrow in the morning. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
